Students who liked power systems, machines, or control theory and want a structured, stable pay ladder.

Entry CTC runs roughly Rs 6-12 LPA fixed at central PSUs, with NTPC and Power Grid running among the highest packages once allowances stack up, but Electrical is one of the toughest branches for a PSU-shortlist step score.

items.heading: Decide the Actual Reason First
items.text: Decide the actual reason first. A stronger step score for a better PSU rank, a specific specialisation like power electronics or power systems, or a documented target company that only hires postgraduates for the role you want. "Placements felt weak" is not a reason by itself.

items.heading: Pick the Specialisation, Not Just
items.text: Pick the specialisation, not just the institute name. Power systems, power electronics, control systems, and the newer VLSI/microelectronics-leaning M.Tech tracks lead to very different job markets. A vague "M.Tech Electrical" without a chosen depth area competes worse than a sharp specialisation.

items.heading: Check the Step Score Band
items.text: Check the step score band for your target IIT/NIT honestly. IIT M.Tech admission for Electrical commonly needs a step score in the 750-850 range for general category, depending on the institute and specialisation. A borderline score into a lower-ranked program is a different bet than a strong score into a top-tier lab.

items.heading: Compare Against the Step
items.text: Compare against the step-PSU alternative before committing two years. The same step score that gets you into a mid-tier M.Tech program might also qualify you for PSU shortlisting at roughly Rs 6-12 LPA starting. Run the actual number against both doors before assuming the degree is the safer choice.
